words.technical: Gold fell close to 9% on the week, and its trend score is negative at every horizon from one month to one year. Price now sits at the very bottom of its 252-day range, so there is no support from recent history. Daily volatility is elevated, which is why next week's range is unusually wide. The Wait stance flips only if price recovers a long way.
words.macro: Gold remained near its lowest level since September 2025. Gold dropped below $3,650.00 an ounce to fresh 14-month lows on Thursday.
words.long_term: Gold had a strong multi-year run that this week's rate-hike repricing has sharply interrupted. The structural case now depends on whether real rates and the dollar keep rising or the Federal Reserve's path softens.

eoy_scenarios.central: Gold stabilises after the violent week and chops sideways as markets wait for the late-November inflation data and the December Fed meeting, finishing the year inside the central band.
eoy_scenarios.upside: Inflation data or Fed language cools the rate-hike pricing, the dollar eases, and a sharp short-covering rebound lifts gold back toward its autumn levels.
eoy_scenarios.downside: A December hike plus a still-strong dollar extends forced selling across metals, and gold keeps sliding below the central band into year-end.

words.technical: Silver lost roughly a sixth of its value on the week, the steepest drop of the seven instruments. Every trend horizon is negative and price sits at the floor of its 252-day range. It is also the most volatile instrument on the page by daily movement, so the range for next week is very wide.
words.macro: Silver has meantime fallen 9 weeks in the past 12, BullionVault noted a week earlier. Metals sold off on expectations for additional Federal Reserve interest rate increases.
words.long_term: Silver trades as both a monetary and an industrial metal, so it amplifies gold's moves in either direction. After a drop this size the structural picture is one of high volatility, not a settled trend.

eoy_scenarios.central: Silver stays volatile but finds a base as selling exhausts itself, ending the year inside the central band well below its autumn levels.
eoy_scenarios.upside: A fade in rate-hike pricing and a recovery in risk appetite triggers a sharp rebound, because silver's moves are larger than gold's in both directions.
eoy_scenarios.downside: Continued forced liquidation across metals and a firmer dollar push silver through the lower band before year-end.

words.technical: Oil fell about 5.6% on the week, its third straight weekly decline, yet its trend score is only mildly negative and price remains near the middle of its 252-day range. That is why oil is the one risk asset on the page with a Flat reading: the computed signals show a market drifting, not collapsing.
words.macro: Brent and WTI were on track for a third consecutive weekly drop. Oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz have returned to roughly pre-war levels. Tension persisted around Iran's intensifying attacks on tankers transiting the Strait of Hormuz. Brent was on track for a near 5% decline for the week. WTI rose 1.18 per cent to close at $83.41 a barrel on Friday.
words.long_term: Oil is caught between a geopolitical risk premium in the Gulf and recovering export flows. Which of the two dominates sets the structural direction.

eoy_scenarios.central: Export flows keep normalising and Gulf tension stays contained, leaving oil range-bound inside the central band through year-end.
eoy_scenarios.upside: Renewed attacks on shipping or a disruption in Gulf exports re-inject a supply premium and push oil above the central band.
eoy_scenarios.downside: A deeper equity sell-off dents demand expectations while supply keeps recovering, and oil slips below the central band.

words.long_term: Bitcoin is behaving as a high-beta risk asset tied to technology equities and liquidity. The structural picture depends on whether fund flows stabilise once equity volatility settles.

eoy_scenarios.upside: A relief rally in technology shares and a return of fund inflows lifts bitcoin sharply back above the central band.
eoy_scenarios.downside: Continued fund outflows and a deeper equity drawdown push bitcoin through the lower band.

words.technical: The S&P 500 fell about 8.6% on the week, a large move for a broad index. Its trend score is negative at the three shorter horizons while the one-year trend is still slightly positive, and price sits in the lower part of its 252-day range. The Wait stance flips to Flat only on a recovery of roughly a few percent.
words.macro: Both the S&P 500 and Dow finished in correction territory. The S&P 500 lost 8.6%, the Dow surrendered 8%, and the Russell 2000 fell 7.5%. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 10.73%, with all 30 constituent stocks declining.
words.long_term: The index remains positive over a one-year horizon, but concentration in a handful of technology leaders means the sell-off in that group now dominates the whole index's direction.

eoy_scenarios.central: Volatility stays high but the index stabilises after the correction and finishes the year inside the central band.
eoy_scenarios.upside: Technology leaders recover and rate-hike fears ease, lifting the index back toward its earlier highs by year-end.
eoy_scenarios.downside: The technology rout broadens and a December rate increase tightens conditions, taking the index below the central band.

words.technical: The dollar index rose a modest 0.4% on the week but its trend is positive at every horizon and price sits at the very top of its 252-day range. Daily volatility is the lowest on the page, so even small moves are meaningful. The Hold stance carries a historical hit rate only a little above a coin flip.
words.macro: The dollar remained near its strongest level in 19 months. Markets priced a 93.9% probability of a 25-basis-point increase in December.
words.long_term: The dollar is being driven by policy divergence, with the Federal Reserve now expected to tighten. The structural picture holds while that expectation holds.

eoy_scenarios.central: The dollar stays firm but range-bound as the December hike is largely priced, finishing the year inside the central band.
eoy_scenarios.upside: A hawkish Fed message and continued safe-haven demand push the dollar above the central band.
eoy_scenarios.downside: Softer inflation data or a more cautious Fed leads to profit-taking in a crowded position, dropping the dollar below the central band.

week_summary: A broad, synchronised sell-off: equities, precious metals, crypto and oil all fell hard while the dollar firmed. The common thread in the coverage was a technology-led equity rout alongside markets pricing a Federal Reserve rate increase in December. Six of seven instruments sit in the Wait or Flat stance and only the dollar holds a Hold. After a week this one-sided, the computed ranges are wide, and the track record shows the Wait stance has been right less often than a coin flip.
